messages:
alex_k: Hey team — proposing a storage "slimdown" for console telemetry. We keep the minimal indexed attributes in events_v2 and move the freeform `event_payload` JSON into a compressed blobs table (or object store) for cold access. Goal: drop storage cost ~40% and reduce p99 query tail for dashboard tiles. Thoughts?

maria_w: How will dashboard tiles behave during the cutover? recompute heavy tiles will be the pain point. :thinking_face: 

alex_k: Plan: two-pronged — 1) read adapter that serves requests from v2 and falls back to blobs table when populate=false, 2) async recompute pipeline to warm derived tiles post-migration. Dashboard shows "stale" indicator until recompute completes. We keep stale reads as an explicit option for UX.

sanjay_p: Dual-write window + read-adapter seems safest. We should add an opt-in header so we can test tenants without changing SDKs. e.g. `X-Telemetry-Storage: v2-preview`. Also watch GROUP BY queries — moving the large JSON out may break some legacy ad-hoc analytics unless we provide a lateral join helper.

alex_k: Agree. Draft migration orchestrator: per-tenant windows, rate-limited backfills, and a pause/resume API. Sample header and backfill job: 
```
# request header to enable read-adapter for a tenant
X-Telemetry-Storage: v2-preview
```
Backfill command: 
```
python tooling/backfill_telemetry.py --tenant=acme --window=2025-03-01T00:00:00Z..2025-03-08T00:00:00Z --rate=200/s
```
Backfill SQL (chunked): 
```sql
INSERT INTO events_v2 (tenant_id, ts, attrs_hash, attrs_compressed)
SELECT tenant_id, ts, md5(event_payload)::uuid, compress(event_payload)
FROM legacy_events WHERE tenant_id = $1 AND ts BETWEEN $2 AND $3
```

ella: Need an estimated slot-hour and egress cost for that backfill. Also we must consider KV cache invalidation for per-route prefix caches — backfill will change route-level aggregates and could thrash the cache.

ryan_ops: I can run the backfill from infra side. Will schedule as a controlled job with concurrency limits + total token/row rate. We should gate by a feature flag per-tenant so we can pause if SLOs slip.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy telem-read-adapter v2 to prod-5% group started at 2025-03-03T04:00Z :rocket:

maria_w: UX ask: Console should expose migration state per-tenant + a progress bar + ability to pause/resume. Also surface estimated recompute time per dashboard tile and list of affected tiles. That will help PMs plan customer comms.

alex_k: Will add Console endpoints: `GET /v1/migration/{tenant}` and `POST /v1/migration/{tenant}/pause`. Feature flag naming: `telemetry_storage.v2` with rollout stages: preview->canary->gradual->complete. We’ll emit events to `console-audit` and `telemetry-migration` streams for visibility.

sanjay_p: Set SLO gates: if query p99 increases > 20% for same cost bucket, auto-pause migration for that tenant and alert #eng-oncall. Also fallback policy: if read-adapter sees > 5% missing attrs for aggregator queries, route to legacy store for that request.

alex_k: Canary plan: 5% tenants for 48 hours, monitor p50/p95/p99, backfill lag, and cost delta. If green, escalate to 25% for 24h, then 100% staggered by region. Add a precheck that ensures no active long-running analytic job for a tenant in the window.

ella: For aggregations, suggest a sample lateral rewrite so dashboards don't fail: 
```sql
SELECT r.route_id, sum((d.attrs->>'duration')::int) AS total_ms
FROM events_v2 r
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT jsonb_extract_path_text(decompress(d.attrs_compressed),'duration') AS duration
) d ON true
GROUP BY r.route_id;
```
This avoids scanning legacy blob table for every query.

ryan_ops: We'll add a maintenance flag we can set during backfill for heavy tenants: `tenant_maintenance: true` — Console will surface it. Also will rate-limit backfills to keep cluster headroom.

maria_w: Perfect. Can someone add this sequence and the abort conditions to the migration runbook? I'll want a runbook snippet in the Console UI for customers to self-serve pause. :thumbsup:

alex_k: On it — I'll open the runbook PR and wire Console progress endpoints. Thanks all — tagging follow-ups: @sanjay_p for SLO gates, @ryan_ops for backfill infra, @ella for query rewrites and cost estimate.
